data.title: U.S. Treasury Prices Fall as Stock Rally Weakens Safe-Haven Demand
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. Treasury prices fell when trading resumed after the Thanksgiving holiday, as gains in stocks weakened demand for safe-haven assets. Yields across maturities rose 6 to 8 basis points, with the 10-year yield at 4.93%; yields were near session highs at Friday’s early close.

TD Securities strategist Prashant Newnaha said increased risk appetite was the main driver of the modest rise in bond yields. For weeks, the artificial intelligence trade has been a major influence on the Treasury market: gains in AI stocks have weighed on bond demand, and the reverse has also occurred. Whether hundreds of billions of dollars in AI spending generate returns matters for the U.S. economy and the Federal Reserve’s response to high inflation.

The latest move gave back some of Treasuries’ earlier gains, which had followed a stock sell-off driven by growing doubts about the AI trade and a reduction in traders’ bets on Fed rate hikes. Overnight index swaps showed a 100% probability of two Fed rate hikes by March next year and nearly a 90% chance of a third by midyear. Two weeks earlier, swaps indicated expectations for three hikes by September next year and a 35% chance of a fourth. Some traders now expect the Fed to shift toward easing later next year as the effects of rate hikes and falling stocks weigh on the world’s largest economy.

Jefferies economist Mohit Kumar said the Fed’s December policy meeting could mark the peak in hawkishness and a turning point for markets.

Technology shares stabilized on Friday. The Nasdaq 100 rose 2.6%, the S&P 500 gained 1.6%, and Nvidia rose 0.8% after falling as much as 2.6%.

At 2 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, the two-year Treasury yield was up 6.2 basis points at 4.7036%; the five-year yield rose 7.3 basis points to 4.742%; the 10-year yield gained 7.6 basis points to 4.9296%; and the 30-year yield increased 7.3 basis points to 5.3213%. The five-year/30-year spread was little changed at 57.75 basis points, while the two-year/10-year spread widened about 1.3 basis points to 22.39 basis points.

For post-holiday trading, the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association recommended a 2 p.m. New York close for dollar-denominated bonds. Bloomberg’s bond index used 1 p.m. prices for the day’s close, when U.S. stocks finished trading; CME interest-rate and stock-index futures ended trading 15 minutes later.

data.title: Capital Economics’ Jonas Goltermann: Flat Treasury Yield Curve Signals Tightening Risks
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Capital Economics Chief Market Economist Jonas Goltermann said the U.S. Treasury yield curve is at its flattest level since early last year. Short-term Treasury yields remain high relative to long-term yields, reflecting the market’s view that tight monetary policy will weigh on economic growth and corporate profits.

data.title: STOCKS | Anthropic Swings in First Trading Week, Closes Above $83 IPO Price
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Anthropic PBC ended its first week on Nasdaq above its $83 IPO price. Shares rose nearly 11% in New York on Friday to close at $91.88, their highest closing level since trading began on November 19, recovering after closing below the IPO price in each of the previous two sessions.

Risk appetite picked up after the Thanksgiving holiday, and Anthropic joined a broad advance in U.S. stocks. The company, led by Dario Amodei, had a market capitalization of about $1.7 trillion, below its peak of more than $2 trillion on its first trading day, when shares touched $115.10.

data.title: Verizon in Talks to Acquire Fidium in Deal Valued at About $6 Billion
data.description: According to Sina Finance, citing the Financial Times, Verizon is negotiating a deal valued at about $6 billion to acquire Fidium, a fiber broadband operator. Talks between Verizon and Fidium’s owner are ongoing, and the deal could be reached in the coming weeks. Other bidders could emerge, and there is no guarantee the negotiations will result in a deal. Verizon declined to comment, while Fidium and its owners, Searchlight and BCI, did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

data.title: GTA VI’s Record Launch Puts Human-Made Games in Focus
data.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI arrived after 13 years in development and broke records, Bloomberg reported. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said Rockstar’s game was made without generative AI.

Gordon Bellamy, director of ethics at the USC School of Cinematic Arts, discussed the value of human-made content, the possibility that GTA VI’s launch could reshape holiday spending across the gaming industry, and lessons for smaller studios.

data.title: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Other Banks Near $400 Million Municipal Bond Lawsuit Settlement
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and other Wall Street banks are nearing a settlement of a municipal bond price-manipulation lawsuit for more than $400 million. The proposed amount, negotiated in recent days, could be submitted to a court soon, according to a person familiar with the matter. It is a fraction of the billions of dollars in damages sought by plaintiffs.

The settlement would end a long-running federal class action that advanced to the doorstep of the U.S. Supreme Court and was preparing to go to a jury trial. Local governments, led by Philadelphia, alleged that the banks conspired to artificially raise rates on certain debt instruments and profited at taxpayers’ expense. Representatives of the cities and banks declined to comment on the settlement talks. The financial institutions have denied the allegations in court.

data.title: UK Steel Sector Says UK-EU Deal Favors EU Exporters
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Britain’s steel sector is urging the government to reverse part of its recent deal with the European Union, saying it gives the bloc’s steel exporters an unfair advantage over UK peers.

data.title: Colombian Peso Retreats as Risks Challenge Carry-Fueled Rally
data.description: According to Bloomberg, the Colombian peso is headed for its worst month in more than four years as domestic and international risks weigh on one of the year’s most resilient currencies.
